text:
Among the following, the molecule expected
to be stabilized by anion formation is :

$C_{2}, O_{2}$, NO, $F_{2}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A molecule is stabilised by forming an anion when the added electron enters a bonding molecular orbital, so the bond order rises.

$\mathrm{C}{}_{2}$ (12 electrons): $σ1s^{2}\qquad σ^{\ast }1s^{2}σ2s^{2}σ^{\ast }2s^{2}π2p_{x}^{2}=π2p_{y}^{2}$, bond order $=\dfrac{8-4}{2}=2$. In $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ the 13th electron enters the bonding $σ2p_{z}$ orbital, so bond order $=\dfrac{9-4}{2}=2.5$: stabilised.

$\mathrm{NO}$ (15 electrons) has one electron in $π^{\ast }2p$, bond order $=\dfrac{10-5}{2}=2.5$. In $\mathrm{NO}{}^{-}$ the extra electron also enters $π^{\ast }2p$, bond order $=\dfrac{10-6}{2}=2$: destabilised.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ (16 electrons), bond order $=\dfrac{10-6}{2}=2$; $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ has a third $π^{\ast }2p$ electron, bond order $=\dfrac{10-7}{2}=1.5$: destabilised.

$\mathrm{F}{}_{2}$ (18 electrons), bond order $=\dfrac{10-8}{2}=1$; in $\mathrm{F}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ the extra electron enters $σ^{\ast }2p_{z}$, bond order $=\dfrac{10-9}{2}=0.5$: destabilised.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

text:
The one that will show optical activity is :

(en = ethane-1,2-diamine)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In each figure the four corners of the rectangle are the equatorial positions of the octahedron (diagonally opposite corners are trans to each other) and the two vertical lines are the axial positions.

(A) is mer-$\mathrm{MA}{}_{3}\mathrm{B}{}_{3}$, (B) is trans-$[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}\mathrm{A}{}_{2}]$ and (D) is trans-$\mathrm{MA}{}_{2}\mathrm{B}{}_{4}$. Each has a mirror plane: in (A) the plane containing the three A ligands, and in (B) and (D) the equatorial plane. None of them is optically active.

In (C) en spans two cis equatorial positions; the equatorial A is trans to one N of en, the equatorial B is trans to the other N, and the axial A is trans to the axial B.

The only planes that could carry the en ring into itself are the equatorial plane and the vertical plane bisecting the en ring. The equatorial plane exchanges the axial A and B, and the vertical plane exchanges the equatorial A and B, so neither is a mirror plane and there is no centre of symmetry.

The complex in (C) is therefore non-superimposable on its mirror image and shows optical activity.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

text:
The given plots represent the variation of the
concentration of a reactant R with time for two
different reactions (i) and (ii). The respective
orders of the reactions are :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $1^{st}$ order reaction, we know

$\ln \frac{R_{0}}{R_{T}}=kt$

$\Rightarrow$ $\ln R_{0}$ - $\ln R_{t}$ = kt

$\Rightarrow$ $\ln R_{t}$ = - kt + $\ln R_{0}$

So,  $\ln R_{t}$ vs t is a straight line with negative slope.

$\therefore$ First graph represent $1^{st}$ order reaction.

For zero order reaction, we know

$R_{0} - R_{t} = kt$

$\therefore$  $R_{t} = - kt + R_{0}$

So,  $R_{t}$ vs t is a straight line with negative slope.

$\therefore$ Second graph represent zero order reaction.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

text:
For a reaction,

$N_{2}(g) + 3H_{2}(g)$ $\to$ $2NH_{3}(g)$ ;

identify dihydrogen $(H_{2})$ as a limiting reagent
in the following reaction mixtures.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}+3\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$, $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$ is the limiting reagent when the moles of $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$ are less than $3\times$ the moles of $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$.

(A) $56\text{g}\mathrm{N}{}_{2}=2\text{mol}$ needs $6\text{mol}\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$; $10\text{g}\mathrm{H}{}_{2}=5\text{mol}<6$, so $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$ is limiting.

(B) $14\text{g}\mathrm{N}{}_{2}=0.5\text{mol}$ needs $1.5\text{mol}\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$; $4\text{g}\mathrm{H}{}_{2}=2\text{mol}>1.5$, so $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$ is limiting.

(C) $28\text{g}\mathrm{N}{}_{2}=1\text{mol}$ needs $3\text{mol}\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$; $6\text{g}\mathrm{H}{}_{2}=3\text{mol}$ exactly, so the mixture is stoichiometric and neither is limiting.

(D) $35\text{g}\mathrm{N}{}_{2}=1.25\text{mol}$ needs $3.75\text{mol}\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$; $8\text{g}\mathrm{H}{}_{2}=4\text{mol}>3.75$, so $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$ is limiting.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

solution.body:
$P_{M}^{0}$ = 450 mmHg and $P_{N}^{0}$ = 700 mmHg

Also we know,

text:
Aniline dissolved in dilute HCl is reacted with
sodium nitrite at 0ºC. This solution was added
dropwise to a solution containing equimolar
mixture of aniline and phenol in dil. HCl. The
structure of the major product is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Aniline in dil. HCl with $\mathrm{NaNO}{}_{2}$ at 0 °C gives benzenediazonium chloride:

$\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}+\mathrm{NaNO}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{HCl}\longrightarrow \mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}+\mathrm{NaCl}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

This acidic solution is added to aniline and phenol in dil. HCl. Phenol couples only as the phenoxide ion, in mildly alkaline medium; in acid it stays un-ionised and does not couple, so $p$-hydroxyazobenzene (A) is not formed.

Aniline couples with the diazonium ion in mildly acidic medium at its para position, giving $p$-aminoazobenzene (yellow dye).


[IMG]

Any diazoaminobenzene (B) formed by attack at nitrogen rearranges to $p$-aminoazobenzene in the acid medium, so it is not the final major product.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

text:
The element having greatest difference between
its first and second ionization energies, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Electronic configuration of Potassium (K) :

$1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}4s^{1}$

After first ionisation enthalpy its configuration becomes :

$1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}$

which is an inert gas configuration. To remove an electron from inert gas configuration requires very high energy.

So Potassium (K) have high difference in the first
ionisation and the second ionisation energy as
it achieve stable noble gas configuration
after first ionisation.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

text:
For any given series of spectral lines of atomic
hydrogen, let $\Delta v^{_}=$ $\Delta v–_{\max }-\Delta v–_{\min }$ be the difference
in maximum and minimum frequencies in
$cm^{–1}$. The ratio $\frac{\Delta v–_{Lyman}}{\Delta v–_{Balmer}}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

$v–=RZ^{2}\left (\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right )$

$\therefore$ For Lyman series,

$\Delta v–_{Lyman}$ = $\Delta v–_{\max }-\Delta v–_{\min }$

= $\left [\frac{1}{1}-\frac{1}{\infty }\right ]-\left [\frac{1}{1}-\frac{1}{4}\right ]$

= $\frac{1}{4}$

$\therefore$ For Balmer series,

$\Delta v–_{Balmer}$ = $\Delta v–_{\max }-\Delta v–_{\min }$

= $\left [\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{\infty }\right ]-\left [\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{9}\right ]$

= $\frac{1}{9}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{\Delta v–_{Lyman}}{\Delta v–_{Balmer}}$ = $\frac{\frac{1}{4}}{\frac{1}{9}}$ = $\frac{9}{4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

text:
The major product of the following reaction is :

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{DCl}$ (1 equiv.) adds to propyne by Markovnikov's rule: $\mathrm{D}{}^{+}$ goes to the terminal carbon, giving the more stable $2^{\circ }$ vinyl cation, which takes $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ to give $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CCl}=\mathrm{CHD}$.

In the addition of $\mathrm{DI}$, $\mathrm{D}{}^{+}$ again adds to the $\mathrm{CHD}$ carbon, because the carbocation then formed on the carbon bearing chlorine, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{C}{}^{+}(\mathrm{Cl})\mathrm{CHD}{}_{2}$, is stabilised by donation of a chlorine lone pair into the empty p orbital.

$\mathrm{I}{}^{-}$ bonds to this carbon, so the product is the geminal dihalide $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{I})(\mathrm{Cl})\mathrm{CHD}{}_{2}$.


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (C).
